items.title: At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see
items.summary: For 16 years I've been watching the skies. It was 16 years ago, back in the first giddy rush of smartphone gaming, that I saw a 30-second trailer for a game set in space. It was a game about a comet, hurtling through the unknown. It wasn't clear what you'd do in this game, whether you'd control the comet itself or the space it moved through. It wasn't clear if this was some kind of arcade game, or a new spin on the endless runner, or even just a kind of cosmic sandbox. All I had was the comet and a name: Faraway. Faraway! I was captivated.
items.t: At last, I've finally played Faraway, an enigma I've been waiting 16 years to see

items.title: Drone Pilots have come to Cyber Knights: Flashpoint, the stealth tactics game's "most complex" class yet, alongside a pet system and the promise of "assassin cats"

They all live in my rucksack, ready and waiting should I need somebody to dupe a security guard or fill the air around me with explosive chaff. All except Clippy, that is. He's too chonky to stuff in a bag, which can make for tricky mission extractions, but he compensates for that with his generous selection of *voice drops six octaves* FULLY LOADED AUTOCANNONS.

With friends like these, who needs human allies? It's time to play stealth tactics sim Cyber Knights: Flashpoint the way it was meant to be played: skulking in a hole while buzzing, clanking mechabastards cleanse the map of any and all defenders. Don't spare the lead, Rosie. You were not built to understand mercy.

items.title: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
items.summary:
In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release."

This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers.

By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana . 

A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.
items.t: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet

Just prior to that, Team Cherry surprised everyone by announcing that the Hollow Knight: Silksong launch was imminent, and Aeternum—and a whole bunch of others —decided the smart move was to just get out of the way.

Well, here we go again. Yesterday, Team Cherry announced that " Cherry Time " is coming on November 27, with "a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow," the Silksong expansion announced in December 2025. Some fans are hoping that means the Sea of Sorrow release date will be announced—or maybe even that it will actually be released.

Whatever's coming, Aeternum says that this time around, it's standing firm.

"Dear Team Cherry," Aeternum wrote in an Official Statement: Part 2 message, riffing on the "Official Statement" it put out in 2025. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong. items.title: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"
items.summary:
The potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have announced. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November , even as the company's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives."

Speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.
items.t: "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director . With thousands of enterable buildings , unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs , and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

"As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, says in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun." 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile , a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System .

items.title: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition
items.summary:
After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. 

25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union said, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

Rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters. 

Despite the vote, the union said it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions…
items.t: Rockstar workers vote overwhelmingly against union recognition

items.title: How to steal the Bravado Banshee in GTA 6
items.summary:
The Bravado Banshee is another one of the cars you'll need to track down for Randy in GTA 6 , but unlike the Pegassi Infernus , this one doesn't involve anything as dodgy as robbing a police lockup. 

You can find this car inside the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom at the north tip of Southside, southwest of Pay 'N' Spray - Salton or east across the road from Ron Gas - Southside. This region is to the northeast of Hamlet. 

There are two showrooms here, so make sure you have the right one, though the other does contain Pfister Growlers, in case you haven't gotten that car for Randy yet, either. Head inside to find the car—if you've played previous GTAs, you'll recognise it as a convertible with a white stripe down the middle. Hop inside, use the key cloner, and drive it through the glass. 

This might damage it a bit, but you can always repair it at Ron Gas nearby, or at the gas station near Randy's shop. Just remember to drive fast, and if the tracker starts to beep, speed up to stop it pinging your location to the cops. Delivering this one gets you 6,500k and a 5k condition bonus as usual if it's in good nick.

items.title: Should you participate in GTA 6's Safe Word mission?
items.summary:
Deciding whether to participate or not in GTA 6 's Safe Word mission is tricky. On the one hand, you don't want to blow your cover, on the other, the setup is incredibly funny. Jason and Lucia head to a mansion to steal a safe, masquerading as pool cleaners, but once Jay heads inside, it's clear that he's actually playing a poolboy in an erotic flick.

While applying lotion to the female performers, Lucia will get increasingly agitated in his earpiece, and then you'll finally have to choose whether to actually participate in the scene or not:

Participate : This will negatively impact your romance with Lucia and since the outcome is the same (Lucia immediately interrupts the scene by setting off a car alarm), Jason doesn't actually do anything. As Rockstar has previously said, you can't cheat on Lucia . After you leave the scene, Lu will be a little angry, but it won't hang over things. Don't Participate : This will positively impact your romance and as above, the car alarm will immediately go off afterwards, ending the scene anyway. Jason will say he needs to go to the bathroom and make his way inside the mansion, continuing the mission to find and steal the safe. So, on the whole, choosing not to participate is better if you care about your romance level and how it might impact things later. If not, say what you will.

items.title: GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights
items.summary:
When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out. But on night one of my playthrough, I clocked some weird streetlights.

Why are some of them turquoise? 

(Image credit: Rockstar) And hey, why are these purple?

Rockstar Rockstar A stylistic choice by Rockstar? Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it. So I DMed my buddy Henry, an honest-to-god Floridian who was also playing GTA 6, and asked what's up. At first he thought strange streetlights in the Key Lento area of the map were special lights meant to not disorient turtles, but those are typically red, so probably not. And that doesn't explain the purple ones.

So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.

"The purple [lights] are definitely real. We have a ton of them down here because whoever is in charge of that in the government bought a bunch of defective lights," the anonymous Floridian responded.

I have mostly noticed purple lights in Crosstown so far. (Image credit: Rockstar) Yes, actual Florida cities are lit by these dubiously dim, yet undeniably cool purple lamps. According to ClickOrlando , residents first started reporting the purple streetlights in 2023. They put up hundreds of these things across the state before they started malfunctioning—it was such a kerfuffle that the government eventually released a statement saying their vendor really screwed the pooch.…
items.t: GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights

items.title: Warhammer Survivors update buffs XP and weapons, nerfs those damn Beasts of Nurgle
items.summary:
If you've played over a hundred hours of Vampire Survivors you've probably forgotten how slow its early progression feels. It certainly seemed that way based on the reaction to Warhammer Survivors from Vampire Survivors veterans, who complained about its grindiness compared to their beloved bullet heaven originator, despite the arc of both games being quite similar. Developers Auroch Digital made Warhammer Survivors in partnership with Vampire Survivors creator Poncle, so of course the two games have a lot in common. 

Other complaints were more valid. The Beasts of Nurgle did have too many hit points, and their ability to regenerate only exacerbated that. The treasure chest-opening animation did take a bit too long. And some of the weapons were undertuned. Fortunately, those issues and more have been addressed in hotfix v2.18 . Here are the highlights:

Balance changes to weapons and enemies, improving weapon damage on select weapons, an aim-assist on the Boltgun and a reduction of max health points on various enemies (including that gargantuan Carnifex!). Added a health bar for enemy minibosses. With the introduction of a new grey Skull Gem, enemies will now always provide some amount of XP. Improved weapon projectile collision on various stages as well as continued improvements to prevent chests dropping at inaccessible locations. Playable champions now break Light Sources when they walk over them. Shortened the Treasure Chest animation, and it is now more common to encounter a rare chest if your luck has been poor. Reduced the volume of the self-destruct alert sound…

items.title: Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027
items.summary:
"Exoprimal is a throwback to weird, experimental early 2000s Capcom ," we wrote of the team-based hero shooter ahead of its launch back in 2023. While ostensibly about battling dinosaurs, "you first go through an interdimensional time portal controlled by a rogue AI, and then you compete in a Hunger Games-style contest against alternate universe versions of yourself for the AI's amusement. That's where the dinosaur killing comes in."

Despite that intriguing premise, the end result was not particularly memorable: Perfectly fine, and with some fantastic ideas, but "more like an early access phase than a finished game," we wrote in our 69% review . And it didn't catch on: A year later, Capcom announced the end of new updates for the game, although the game remained fully playable.

But now that's changing too. Capcom announced today that Exoprimal services will be terminated on September 29, 2027 , at which point the game will become unplayable. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years," Capcom wrote, "and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement."

The sale of seasonal "survival passes," which have been rotating through Exoprimal's four seasons since the end of updates in 2024, has been halted, while the game itself along with all DLC and "other products"—there's quite a lot of it —will be removed from sale on March 30, 2027. After that, the game will tick on—and Capcom hopes you will continue to enjoy it—until the end of the road in September.

It sucks to see games fail, especially when they have the potential…
items.t: Capcom's quirky dinosaur-fighting hero shooter is shutting down in 2027

Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.
